title: Beyond Passive Imitation: On-Policy Mid-Training Distillation for Language Models
abstract: arXiv:2611.13855v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Continual pre-training (CPT) adapts large language models (LLMs) to specialized domains, yet its standard next-token prediction (NTP) objective treats every corpus token as a fixed target, regardless of its utility to the current model. In a controlled study on the same 1B-token mathematical corpus, we observe sharply different outcomes across base models: NTP improves Llama-3.2-3B's performance on mathematical benchmarks but substantially degrades Qwen3-1.7B-Base's performance, indicating that, under a fixed training recipe, the same training sequences can have model-dependent effects. To address this problem, we introduce On-Policy Mid-Training Distillation (OPMD), which reformulates mid-training from offline text imitation into active, query-driven knowledge acquisition. At selected anchor positions, OPMD samples trajectories from the evolving student policy and applies dense token-level reverse-KL rewards from a frozen teacher, train

translated_title: 超越被动模仿：面向语言模型的在线策略中期训练蒸馏
translated_abstract: 持续预训练（CPT）可将大型语言模型（LLM）适配到特定领域，然而其标准的下一词预测（NTP）目标将语料库中的每个词元都视为固定目标，而不考虑其对当前模型的效用。在一项基于相同10亿词元数学语料库的对照研究中，我们观察到不同基础模型之间结果差异显著：NTP提升了Llama-3.2-3B在数学基准上的表现，却显著降低了Qwen3-1.7B-Base的性能，这表明在固定的训练方案下，相同的训练序列可能产生依赖于具体模型的效果。为解决这一问题，我们提出了在线策略中期训练蒸馏（OPMD），将中期训练从离线的文本模仿重新表述为主动的、查询驱动的知识获取。在选定的锚定位置，OPMD从不断演进的学生策略中采样轨迹，并应用来自冻结教师模型的密集词元级反向KL奖励进行训练。
tldr: 该论文提出在线策略中期训练蒸馏（OPMD），将中期训练从被动的离线文本模仿转变为主动的、查询驱动的知识获取，通过从学生策略自采样轨迹并结合教师模型的词元级反向KL奖励，解决了标准下一词预测目标在不同基础模型上效果不一甚至产生负面影响的问题。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes On-Policy Mid-Training Distillation (OPMD), which transforms mid-training from passive offline text imitation into active, query-driven knowledge acquisition by sampling trajectories from the evolving student policy and applying dense token-level reverse-KL rewards from a frozen teacher, addressing the problem that standard next-token prediction can yield inconsistent or even harmful effects across different base models.
